changed.title: Some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 5 gates represents one of two named 5 by 5 graphs (masks 16235582, 16236078) on the one-a-side promise
changed.statement:

  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 5 ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 5 => M.testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can save more than 2n - 5 gates on the one-a-side promise at side 5, on the two graphs the read-once count leaves open; a met step breaks the 2n - 5 pair there.
changed.context: No witness is known to us; this is a search; two NOT gates or an input read twice are possible here. Give a gate list of at most 5 AND, OR and NOT gates of fan-in two for one of the two masks, judged by evaluation on the 25 promise inputs. Each graph needs at least 11 gates without NOT gates (checked floors: the 'at most 10 AND/OR' rows read refuted). The other twenty masks of the first break step are covered by a separate 'none exists' form. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: Five-input monotone f with table 0xeae8e880: some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 9 gates computes f
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 9 ∧ ∀ x : Fin 5 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = Nat.testBit 0xeae8e880 (∑ i : Fin 5, if x i then 2 ^ (i : ℕ) else 0)
changed.unlocks: settles the least AND/OR size of this five-input monotone function at 9; with the checked row that NOT gates save nothing on it, also its least AND/OR/NOT size
changed.context: FIND (beat this). The answer is an object, not an argument: give the gate list (AND/OR, at most two inputs each, at most 9 gates) and decide the equality over all 32 inputs. The best circuit known to us has 10 gates; none with 8 or fewer exists (exhaustive search, computed, not checked); whether 9 is possible is unknown to us. Pattern: methods/find/example-maj3.lean.txt.
changed.sketch: f on five inputs is true when some listed set is all true: 012, 013, 023, 123, 014, 024, 124, 034 (at least three of 0..3, or 4 with two of 0, 1, 2, or 4 with 0 and 3). We hold a 10-gate AND/OR circuit; an exhaustive search of ours found none with 8 or fewer (computed), so 9 is the only open size. Step: give 9 AND or OR gates, fan-in at most two, each reading only earlier wires, output last; judged by evaluating on all 32 inputs against the table, by decide. A hand idea: share the pair products of 0, 1, 2 between the three-of-four part and the part with 4.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 3 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 363 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 7 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 3) (v : Fin 4) => (363 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) 7
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 3 by 4 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 8 AND/OR gates for this graph that shares nothing; we hold none of 7; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 6 (on paper), a gap of 2. The checked twin merge reduces a square graph to a rectangular quotient, and we hold no table off the square beyond 2 by 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 2 left, 3 to 6 right, gate j writes wire 7 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 12 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: A linear-size circuit decodes Fibonacci addresses for keys matching a three-round output prefix
changed.statement:
∀ (k h : Nat), 13 ≤ k → 0 < h → h ≤ k → ∀ c : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc j =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit j)
        (!(word.testBit ((j + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((j + 2) % k))).toNat <<< j)) 0
  let start := fun (row key : Nat) => rot 1 key ^^^ row
  let first := fun (row key : Nat) =>
    (List.range 3).foldl (fun prev roundIndex =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * roundIndex) key ^^^ (c (roundIndex + 1)).val)
      (start row key)
  let q := min h (k - 11)
  let outside := k - (q + 1)
  let Address := Fin (2 ^ outside) × Fin (2 ^ (q + 1))
  let legal := fun (label : Nat) => label &&& (label >>> 1) = 0
  let bits := fun (width number : Nat) =>
    List.ofFn (fun place : Fin width => number.testBit place.val)
  let pack := fun (starting : Nat) =>
    starting % (2 ^ (outside - 1)) +
      ((starting.testBit (k - 1)).toNat <<< (outside - 1))
  let inputs := k + h + outside + (q + 1)
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun tag : Fin (2 ^ (q + 1)) => legal tag.val)).card =
    Nat.fib (q + 3) ∧
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (keyWire : Fin k → Nat),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
    C.size ≤ 8192 * (k + 1) ∧ C.output < inputs + C.size ∧
    (∀ j, keyWire j < inputs + C.size) ∧
    ∀ (u : Fin (2 ^ k)) (y : Fin (2 ^ h)),
      let dataIn := fun (address : Address) =>
        bits k u.val ++ bits h y.val ++ bits outside address.1.val ++ bits (q + 1) address.2.val
      let good := fun (offer : Address) => C.eval (dataIn offer) = true
      let decode := fun (slot : Address) =>
        let wires := C.wires (dataIn slot)
        (List.finRange k).foldl (fun result pos =>
          result ||| ((wires.getD (keyWire pos) false).toNat <<< pos.val)) 0
      (∀ candidate : Address, good candidate →
        legal candidate.2.val ∧ decode candidate < 2 ^ k ∧
        pack (start u.val (decode candidate)) = candidate.1.val ∧
        (first u.val (decode candidate) >>> (k - h)) = y.val) ∧
      (∀ w : Fin (2 ^ k), (first u.val w.val >>> (k - h)) = y.val →
        ∃! witness : Address, good witness ∧ decode witness = w.val)
changed.unlocks: provides a single linear-size validity circuit and raw key wires for each Fibonacci address
changed.context: Fix exterior bits. Branch on the untested bit, then on q lower bits in order. At each fork look one output ahead. Odd square parity gives a child with one feasible successor. Label that child one and the other zero. Reject one at a sole choice and reject failed tests. Label the last fork by its chosen bit. Each passing path has one code without adjacent ones. Four local probes per level and a final full prefix check fit 8192(k+1) gates. Undo the row mix. Gate-price companions cannot exist for this construction as a smaller circuit also meets the ceiling.

changed.title: At most 2+e private rows have distinct profiles outside a narrow column set in an AND/OR region with e at most one entry wire
changed.statement:
∀ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (R : Finset (Fin n)) (B : Finset (Fin m)) (region entry : Finset ℕ) (top : ℕ),
  let raw := n + m
  let sources := R.image (fun sourceRow => sourceRow.val) ∪ B.image (fun sourceCol => n + sourceCol.val)
  let inside := fun (w : ℕ) => raw ≤ w ∧ w - raw ∈ region
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  (∀ firstRow secondRow : Fin n, firstRow ≠ secondRow → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card) →
  (∀ firstCol secondCol : Fin m, firstCol ≠ secondCol → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun row => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack raw C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → region ⊆ Finset.range C.size → top ∈ region →
  entry.card ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ entry, w < raw + top ∧ w ∉ sources ∧ ¬ inside w) →
  (∀ k ∈ region,
    ((gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
     (gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs, w ∈ sources ∨ inside w ∨ w ∈ entry) →
  (∀ k < C.size, k ∉ region → ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs,
    w ∉ sources ∧ (inside w → w = raw + top)) →
  C.output ∉ sources → (inside C.output → C.output = raw + top) →
  (B.card < d → R.card ≤ 2 + entry.card) ∧ (R.card < d → B.card ≤ 2 + entry.card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of private rows or columns whose profiles differ outside a small opposite set
changed.context: Fix an active outside column and vary the active private row. Until the top, outside gates cannot read a private signal, so the entry value depends only on the column. In the region each row induces a monotone unary truth table on that bit, either zero, identity or one. Without an entry there are two constant tables. Equal tables give identical outputs on every outside column, since only the top leaves the region. Fewer than d private columns cannot hide d disagreements. Count the types and exchange sides. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.
